metadata.title: node-lite
metadata.text:
QuickJS plus a small Node.js compatibility layer, to write servers in JavaScript on MLinxOS without
Node itself (about 2.5 MB with TLS, only libc/libm needed, builds in about a minute).

```
bash tests/smoke.sh        # after building; starts the example servers and checks them with curl
build/node-lite example/server.js 8080        # CommonJS
build/node-lite example/server.mjs 8081       # ES modules
```

metadata.title: node-lite > Build
metadata.text:
POSIX only (sockets use epoll), so on Linux or with the Buildroot toolchain:

```
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --target node-lite

# for the MLinxOS target
cmake -S . -B build-target -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$BUILDROOT/output/host/share/buildroot/toolchainfile.cmake
```

`external/quickjs` is QuickJS-ng; `lib/node-lite.js` is embedded into the binary at configure time.

metadata.title: node-lite > What "importing Node libraries" means here
metadata.text:
`require('x')`, `import x from 'x'` and `import { y } from 'node:x'` all resolve, in this order, to:

1. a builtin: `http`, `dns`, `fs`, `fs/promises`, `path`, `os`, `events`, `util`, `assert`, `url`, `querystring`, `buffer`, `timers`, `process`;
2. a relative or absolute file (`.js`, `.cjs`, `.json`, `index.js`, or a directory's `package.json` `"main"`);
3. `node_modules/<name>` searched upwards from the requiring file (plain CommonJS packages).

Globals: `process`, `Buffer`, `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`setImmediate` and their `clear*`, `URL`, `URLSearchParams`,
`TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`, `fetch`, `Headers`, `Response`, `AbortController`/`AbortSignal`, `queueMicrotask`, `structuredClone`, `console` (`log`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`).

QuickJS' own modules are reachable as `qjs:std` and `qjs:os` only from C, so the name `os` is Node's.

metadata.title: node-lite > http
metadata.text:
`http.createServer(handler)` with `listen(port[, host][, cb])`, `close()`, `address()`, and the usual
`req.method/url/headers`, `req.on('data'|'end')`, `res.statusCode/setHeader/writeHead/write/end`.
Limits: HTTP/1.1 with one request per connection (`Connection: close`), no chunked request bodies (answers 501),
headers up to 64 KB and bodies up to 16 MB, no HTTPS server, and no `http.request`/`http.get` client (use `fetch`).

metadata.title: node-lite > dns
metadata.text:
`dns.lookup`, `dns.resolve4` / `dns.resolve` (callbacks) and `dns.promises.lookup|resolve4`, IPv4 only. They use
`getaddrinfo` on a helper thread, so `/etc/hosts`, `/etc/resolv.conf` and `libnss_dns` apply and the event loop keeps
running. On MLinxOS `/etc/resolv.conf` is written by `udhcpc` once Wi-Fi gets an address.

metadata.title: node-lite > fetch
metadata.text:
```js
const res = await fetch('https://www.google.com', { headers: { 'accept-language': 'en' } });
console.log(res.status, res.headers.get('content-type'), (await res.text()).length);
```

`http://` and `https://`, methods, headers, string/Buffer/`URLSearchParams` bodies, redirects (`redirect: 'follow' |
'manual' | 'error'`, up to 20, `Authorization`/`Cookie` dropped across origins), `AbortController`, and the non-standard
`timeout` option (ms, default 60000, `0` disables). `Response` has `status`, `ok`, `headers`, `url`, `redirected`,
`text()`, `json()`, `arrayBuffer()`, `bytes()`, `clone()`. Bodies are buffered (no streams, `Request` objects or
cookies), servers must answer `identity` content (no gzip/br), and failures throw `TypeError: fetch failed` with the
cause in `error.cause` (`ENOTFOUND`, `ECONNREFUSED`, certificate errors, ...).

metadata.title: node-lite > fetch
metadata.text:
HTTPS uses a statically linked copy of mbedTLS 3.6.4 (`external/mbedtls`, TLS 1.2/1.3) and Mozilla's root certificates
embedded from `external/ca/cacert.pem`, so the system needs no TLS library or CA package. Certificates are verified
(expired, self-signed and wrong-host ones are rejected) and the system clock must be roughly right. `SSL_CERT_FILE`
adds extra CAs and `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` disables verification, as in Node. To refresh the CAs, replace
`external/ca/cacert.pem` (from https://curl.se/ca/cacert.pem) and rebuild.

```
build/node-lite example/fetch.js https://www.google.com
build/node-lite example/fetch.js http://google.com        # follows the redirect to https
```

metadata.title: node-lite > Example: vector database with OpenAI embeddings
metadata.text:
`example/vectordb/` is a small vector store plus a script that embeds a set of texts in batches with `fetch` and the
OpenAI API (key from `OPENAI_API_KEY`). It also shows a real run and how to read the scores; see
[`example/vectordb/README.md`](example/vectordb/README.md). Its test, `tests/vectordb_test.js`, needs no key.

metadata.title: node-lite > Not supported
metadata.text:
npm packages that need native addons, `child_process`, `net`, `stream`, `worker_threads`, `crypto`, `zlib`, `fs.createReadStream`.
The `fs` callback and promise forms run the synchronous call and deliver the result on the next tick.

metadata.title: node-lite > Notes
metadata.text:
The vendored QuickJS `js_os_poll` only dispatches among the first N polled fds (N = number of ready fds), so
with more than one `os.setReadHandler` fd a ready socket can be ignored. node-lite registers a single epoll fd
and dispatches itself (`src/net_native.c`, `poller` in `lib/node-lite.js`) instead of patching the library.

metadata.title: Vector database example
metadata.text:
A small vector store plus a batch-embeddings script that uses `fetch` and the OpenAI API. Plain CommonJS, so it
runs on node-lite and on Node 18+.

```
export OPENAI_API_KEY=...                       # read from the environment, never written anywhere
node-lite embed-batch.js --out vectors.json     # embeds docs.json (20 short texts) in batches
node-lite search.js "how does a computer start up" --k 3
node-lite search.js --like space-mars --k 3     # neighbours of a stored item, no API call
```

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `vectordb.js` | `VectorDB`: `add`, `get`, `remove`, `search(vector, k, { filter })` (cosine, brute force), `save`/`load` as JSON |
| `openai.js` | `embedBatch(texts)` and `embedAll(texts, { batchSize })`: `POST /v1/embeddings`, answers re-ordered by `index`, retries on 429 and 5xx with backoff |
| `embed-batch.js` | Reads `--input` (array of strings or `{ id, text, ...metadata }`), embeds it in batches of `--batch` (default 64) and writes the database |
| `search.js` | Embeds the query with the model stored in the database and prints the closest items |

metadata.title: Vector database example
metadata.text:
Options: `--model` (default `text-embedding-3-small`, or `OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL`), `--dims` (shorter vectors for
the `text-embedding-3-*` models), `OPENAI_BASE_URL` for a compatible server.

metadata.title: Vector database example > Searching node-lite's own documentation
metadata.text:
`index-docs.js` is the practical use: it splits the README files of node-lite into one chunk per section
(`chunker.js`: by heading, long sections by paragraph, code blocks kept whole), embeds them in batches with the section
path in front of each text, and stores them in `docs.vec.json`. `search.js` then answers questions with the sections
that match, in any language:

```
node-lite index-docs.js --dry-run                       # prints the 16 chunks, no API call
node-lite index-docs.js                                 # embeds them (needs OPENAI_API_KEY) -> docs.vec.json
node-lite search.js "how do I cancel a fetch?" --db docs.vec.json --k 3
node-lite search.js "cómo valida los certificados https" --db docs.vec.json --k 3
```

`--files a.md,b.md` indexes other Markdown files, so the same two commands work for any documentation folder. Run
`index-docs.js` again after editing the docs: it rebuilds the whole file (a few hundred tokens for these READMEs).

metadata.title: Vector database example > A real run
metadata.text:
Output of `node embed-batch.js --out vectors.json --batch 8` with Node 24 against the OpenAI API
(`text-embedding-3-small`, 20 texts, 3 requests):

```
embedded 8/20
embedded 16/20
embedded 20/20
20 vectors of 1536 dimensions (text-embedding-3-small), 417 tokens, 2.3 s -> vectors.json
```

`vectors.json` is 364 KB (JSON, 7 significant digits per component). Neighbours of stored items with
`search.js --like <id> --k 3` (score = cosine similarity, no API call needed):

metadata.title: Vector database example > A real run
metadata.text:
```
items like linux-boot: The Linux kernel mounts an initramfs, starts init and then launches the system services...
0.506  linux-grub  [linux]  GRUB is the bootloader that loads the kernel image and the initial ramdisk from the disk.
0.282  linux-udev  [linux]  udev creates the device nodes in /dev and tags input devices so applications can find...
0.193  linux-wifi  [linux]  wpa_supplicant authenticates against the access point and udhcpc then requests...

items like space-moon: La Luna orbita la Tierra cada 27 días y su gravedad provoca las mareas de los océanos.
0.347  space-iss   [space]  The International Space Station circles the Earth every ninety minutes with astronauts...
0.237  space-mars  [space]  Mars is a cold desert planet with the tallest volcano in the solar system and two small moons.
0.169  music-piano [music]  El piano tiene ochenta y ocho teclas y un martillo golpea cada cuerda cuando se pulsa...

items like money-bank: A savings account pays a small interest while the bank lends your deposits to other customers.
0.327  money-stocks [finance]  Buying stocks means owning a small part of a company, and its price rises and falls with the market.
0.166  sport-tennis [sports]   Tennis players serve the ball over the net and win points when the opponent cannot return it.
0.120  cook-soup     [cooking]  A good vegetable soup simmers carrots, leeks and potatoes in broth with a little pepper.
```

metadata.title: Vector database example > A real run
metadata.text:
What to read from it:

- The model groups by meaning, not by words: the Spanish text about the Moon lands next to the English ones about the
  space station and Mars, and `cook-pasta` finds `cook-soup`, `cook-bread` and the Spanish `cook-tortilla`.
- Across the 20 items the nearest neighbour always had the same topic (20/20), and 72 % of all top-3 neighbours did.
  The misses have low scores (0.12 to 0.17), so a minimum score (for example 0.25 for this model) is a reasonable cut-off.
- Scores between unrelated texts stay around 0.1 to 0.2, and related ones start around 0.25. Those numbers depend
  on the model and the corpus; pick the threshold from your own data.
- Cost: 417 tokens for the whole corpus. A key that has expired fails at once with
  `OpenAI API 401 ... expired_secret_key` and nothing is written.

metadata.title: Vector database example > Limits
metadata.text:
Brute force is fine up to some tens of thousands of vectors; beyond that it needs an index. Test (no key needed,
it talks to a local stand-in for the API): `node-lite tests/vectordb_test.js`.
